title: IRHash: Efficient Multi-Language Compiler Caching by IR-Level Hashing
problem: Compilation time is a bottleneck in multi-language software development, and existing compiler caches cannot effectively share compilation results across different programming languages and compiler frontends. Developers face repeated recompilation of semantically equivalent code across polyglot projects.
motivation: Reducing compilation time improves developer productivity and accelerates CI/CD pipelines in projects using multiple programming languages.
method: IRHash uses intermediate representation (IR) level hashing to identify semantically equivalent code across different language frontends and compilers. The system normalizes IR representations and computes stable hashes that enable cross-language cache lookups, allowing compilation results to be reused regardless of source language while a shared cache stores and retrieves these hashed IR compilations.
key_novelty: IR-level hashing enables compiler result caching across different programming languages and frontends by matching semantically equivalent intermediate representations rather than source code.
contributions: An IR-level hashing scheme that identifies equivalent intermediate representations across compiler frontends
A multi-language compiler caching system leveraging IR-level hashing
Significant compilation speedups in polyglot codebases
Evaluation demonstrating effectiveness across multiple programming languages
primary_theme: Multi-language compiler caching via IR-level hashing
